passages.text: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone— for kings and all those in authority—so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul is an apostle and teacher of the Gentiles.
Paul urges Timothy and the church to pray.
He says, “First of all, I urge you to pray for all people.”
Offer petitions for everyone.
Offer prayers for everyone.
Offer intercessions for everyone.
Offer thanksgiving for everyone.
Pray for kings.
Pray for all those in authority.
Pray so that we may live peaceful lives.
Pray so that we may live quiet lives.
Live in all godliness.
Live in all dignity.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ οὖν πρῶτον πάντων ποιεῖσθαι δεήσεις προσευχάς ἐντεύξεις εὐχαριστίας ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων ὑπὲρ βασιλέων καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐν ὑπεροχῇ ὄντων ἵνα ἤρεμον καὶ ἡσύχιον βίον διάγωμεν ἐν πάσῃ εὐσεβείᾳ καὶ σεμνότητι

passages.text: This is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
passages.sermon:
God is our Savior.
God sees everything.
God wants what is good.
God is pleased when we do what is good.
God wants every person to be saved.
God wants every person to know the truth.
passages.original: τοῦτο καλὸν καὶ ἀπόδεκτον ἐνώπιον τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ ὃς πάντας ἀνθρώπους θέλει σωθῆναι καὶ εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave Himself as a ransom for all—the testimony that was given at just the right time.
passages.sermon:
There is one God.
There is one mediator between God and people.
This mediator is the man Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus gave Himself as a ransom for everyone.
God gave this testimony at the right time.
passages.original: Εἷς γὰρ Θεός εἷς καὶ μεσίτης Θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων ἄνθρωπος Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ὁ δοὺς ἑαυτὸν ἀντίλυτρον ὑπὲρ πάντων τὸ μαρτύριον καιροῖς ἰδίοις

passages.text: For this reason I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a faithful and true teacher of the Gentiles. I am telling the truth; I am not lying about anything.
passages.sermon:
God appointed me for this purpose.
God made me a preacher.
God made me an apostle.
God made me a teacher of the Gentiles.
I teach faith and truth.
I am telling the truth.
I am not lying.
passages.original: εἰς ὃ ἐτέθην ἐγὼ κῆρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος ἀλήθειαν λέγω οὐ ψεύδομαι διδάσκαλος ἐθνῶν ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ

passages.text: Therefore I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dissension.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy as an apostle and teacher of the Gentiles.
Paul gives instructions for Christian worship.
Paul wants men to pray in every place.
Paul wants men to lift up holy hands when they pray.
Paul wants men to pray without anger.
Paul wants men to pray without arguing or dissension.
passages.original: Βούλομαι οὖν προσεύχεσθαι τοὺς ἄνδρας ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ ἐπαίροντας ὁσίους χεῖρας χωρὶς ὀργῆς καὶ διαλογισμοῦ

passages.text: Likewise, I want the women to adorn themselves with respectable apparel, with modesty, and with self-control, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes, but with good deeds, as is proper for women who profess to worship God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to Timothy about how Christians should behave in worship.
Paul addresses women who profess to worship God.
Paul wants these women to dress themselves in respectable clothing.
He wants them to show modesty.
He wants them to have self-control.
He does not want them to adorn themselves with braided hair.
He does not want them to wear gold.
He does not want them to wear pearls.
He does not want them to wear expensive clothes.
He wants them to adorn themselves with good deeds.
This is proper for women who claim to worship God.
passages.original: Ὡσαύτως καὶ γυναῖκας ἐν καταστολῇ κοσμίῳ μετὰ αἰδοῦς καὶ σωφροσύνης κοσμεῖν ἑαυτάς μὴ ἐν πλέγμασιν καὶ χρυσίῳ ἢ μαργαρίταις ἢ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ ἀλλ’ ὃ πρέπει γυναιξὶν ἐπαγγελλομέναις θεοσέβειαν δι’ ἔργων ἀγαθῶν

passages.text: A woman must learn in quietness and full submissiveness.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy about how men and women should behave in the church.
Paul says a woman must learn quietly.
She must be in full submission.
She should not speak out or take authority while learning.
She should listen and accept instruction with respect.
passages.original: Γυνὴ ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ μανθανέτω ἐν πάσῃ ὑποταγῇ

passages.text: I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul gives instructions for Christian worship.
Paul addresses the role of women in the church.
Paul does not permit a woman to teach a man.
Paul does not permit a woman to have authority over a man.
Paul instructs a woman to remain quiet.
passages.original: διδάσκειν δὲ γυναικὶ οὐκ ἐπιτρέπω οὐδὲ αὐθεντεῖν ἀνδρός ἀλλ’ εἶναι ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ

passages.text: For Adam was formed first, and then Eve.
passages.sermon: Adam was formed first.\r\nGod created Adam before Eve.\r\nThen God formed Eve.
passages.original: Ἀδὰμ γὰρ πρῶτος ἐπλάσθη εἶτα Εὕα

passages.text: And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression.
passages.sermon: Adam was not deceived.\r\nThe woman was deceived.\r\nThe woman fell into transgression.
passages.original: καὶ Ἀδὰμ οὐκ ἠπατήθη ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἐξαπατηθεῖσα ἐν παραβάσει γέγονεν

passages.text: Women, however, will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes about women.
Women can be saved.
God uses childbearing as a way for women to be saved.
Women must continue in faith.
Women must continue in love.
Women must continue in holiness.
Women must have self-control.
passages.original: σωθήσεται δὲ διὰ τῆς τεκνογονίας ἐὰν μείνωσιν ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ καὶ ἁγιασμῷ μετὰ σωφροσύνης
